newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-JADEJA DENIED CENTURY AS W.INDIES AND INDIA DRAW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JADEJA DENIED CENTURY AS W.INDIES AND INDIA DRAW.

text.p: Indian opening batsman Ajay Jadeja came within a whisker of his maiden test century as the fourth test between the West Indies and India ended in a predictable draw on Tuesday.

Jadeja's eagerness got the better of him when he was run out for 96 as India, replying to the West Indies' first innings total of 333 for nine declared, reached 212 for two at the close on the final day.

A draw had been the only likely result after rain washed out the first three days' play. The West Indies lead the series 1-0 after their 38-run win in Barbados in the third test with the final match to come in Guyana later this month.

Jadeja was out going for an impossible second run after playing a ball to third man. He was clearly out of his ground when Stuart Williams returned the ball to wicket-keeper Courtney Browne, who swiftly removed the bails.
Playing his first innings of the series, Jadeja's brilliant performance dominated the day. He batted for 250 minutes, facing 212 balls and striking seven fours and two sixes.

Jadeja shared in a first wicket stand of 97 with Venkata Laxman as the opening pair, resuming from three without loss at lunch, survived an aggressive opening by Curtley Ambrose and Ian Bishop to bat the entire afternoon session.

In the first over after the break, Laxman, who only kept his place in the side because Navjot Sidhu was unfit, was out as he edged a Courtney Walsh ball to Browne. His knock of 56 included five fours.
The consistent Rahul Dravid, who shared a second wicket partnership of 101 with Jadeja, was 37 not out at the close with Sunil Joshi on 10.
Brian Lara, who hit a world record 375 on the same ground against England three years ago, was named man-of-the-match after his 103 on Monday.
The West Indies, 252 for seven overnight, declared 25 minutes before lunch as a fever-stricken Franklyn Rose, their leading wicket-taker in the series, was not asked to bat.
Browne and Ambrose added 43 before Ambrose (21) edged Abey Kuruvilla to wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia to give the fast bowler his second wicket of the match.
During his innings, the Antiguan paceman had reached 1,000 runs in test cricket when he pulled left arm spinner Joshi for four.
Browne surpassed his previous test best of 34 as he reached 39 not out with captain Walsh, who was out after skying the ball to Dravid to give Joshi his third wicket.
Joshi ended with three for 76, the best Indian figures.
